_comment: The adversarial catalogue for the Verifiable Intent connector. Every case here must be exercised by tests/test_mastercard_vi_provider.py and must fail for the reason recorded, not merely fail. The test asserts that the catalogue and the implemented cases are the same set, so adding a case here without implementing it — or implementing one without recording it — breaks the build.

cases.description: A complete autonomous L1+L2 delegation for two approved suppliers, USD up to 20,000.00, with the correctly paired open checkout and payment mandates.
Layer 1 has already expired, so the root of the chain is no longer current.
The user's mandate has expired; the delegation it expressed is over.
The mandate is dated beyond the recommended clock skew, so its validity window has not begun.

Layer 1 expires before Layer 2 was issued. Both layers still pass the reference verifier, so a Layer-2-only reading of validity would wave this through; the effective intersection is empty and there is no instant at which the chain delegates anything.
Layer 1 is signed by a key that is not the one provisioned for that issuer and kid.
No trusted key is provisioned for the issuer at all, so the signature cannot be accepted.
The claim names one issuer while carrying a credential issued by another.
The mandate was addressed to a different agent platform than this principal is provisioned under.
The chain verifies, but the delegated agent key belongs to some other agent — a valid credential is not evidence that it is this principal's.
The delegated agent key was bound to this principal and has since been revoked.
Nothing ties this Inntris principal to any Verifiable Intent delegate.
The mandate's sd_hash binds to a different Layer 1 than the one presented.
The payment mandate's conditional_transaction_id does not hash to the checkout mandate's disclosure, so the pair is not bound.
The claim names a mandate-pair reference that is not this credential's.
The presented material is not an SD-JWT serialization.
Layer 3 material is presented; this release does not verify it and refuses rather than ignoring it.
An immediate-mode Layer 2 confirms final values and delegates to no agent, so it is not a source of delegated authority.
Layer 2 omits the exp claim the draft marks REQUIRED; the reference implementation tolerates it and Inntris does not.
Every approved payee is withheld, so no proposed payee can be shown to satisfy the allowlist.
The mandate carries a cumulative budget cap, which needs a per-mandate spend ledger this release does not keep.
The mandate authorises repeated agent-managed purchases, which needs occurrence accounting this release does not keep.
The payment mandate carries a constraint type outside the pinned draft's registry, which cannot be evaluated at all.
The delegation is denominated in a currency this release cannot enforce.
The amount range carries a lower bound Inntris has nowhere to enforce; half a constraint is not the constraint.
The pinned reference implementation cannot be loaded, so verification cannot run and success is never reported.
No claim at all. The provider reports an unverified resolution instead of inventing one.
The delegation verifies and the organisation's own policy still blocks the act. A valid chain is never by itself an Inntris ALLOW.
